case_title: Hariprasad @ Kishan Sahu v. State of Chhattisgarh
neutral_facts: The deceased, Bisahu Singh, went to the forest on 22.07.2003 to collect wood but did not return. His wife, Ganeshi Bai, found him in a semi-conscious state in the verandah of their house the next morning. He was taken to the hospital, where he died on 23.07.2003. The post-mortem was conducted on 24.07.2003, and the body was sent for chemical examination to the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) on 18.09.2003. The FSL report, received on 10.08.2004, indicated the presence of Organophosphorous insecticide and Quinolphos in the deceased's viscera. The FIR was registered on 03.11.2004. The prosecution alleged that the accused, Hariprasad, had administered poison in the form of an herb mixed into liquor, leading to the deceased's death. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 of the IPC, but the High Court confirmed the conviction. The Supreme Court, however, set aside the conviction, finding that the prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the deceased died from poison administered by the accused, and that the delay in registering the FIR was not fatal to the prosecution's case.
